text:
alex: Quick sync — need to lock acceptance criteria + launch gates for private deploys where customer manages egress/BGP. Customers keep asking for 'bring-your-own-egress' and we need clear scope for initial rollout. TL;DR: propose minimal working set + blockers.

priya: Product asks — must support: customer-provided egress IP, per-tenant BGP peering, audit-ready logs, documented rollback. Want canary plan and explicit metrics.

kai: From eng-platform: agree. We need a clear network interface contract: interface name, expected CIDR ranges, NAT vs no-NAT behavior, and the healthcheck endpoints we'll probe. Proposed acceptance checklist below.

sam: Security notes: require KMS integration for control plane keys, mTLS for control plane <-> customer device, explicit rules about packet capture and PII. Need threat-model signoff before GA.

natalie: SE: customers will test with a simple FRR config and expect example BGP configs in docs. We should include a troubleshooting matrix for common failures (no route, ASN mismatch, flapping).

alex: Proposed minimum acceptance criteria:
- Control plane establishes mTLS connection with client cert and validates CN
- Customer can provide a static outbound egress IP per-tenant (or small pool)
- BGP session establishes (our ASN peered with customer ASN) and customer prefixes are accepted/announced
- Healthcheck probes to /health and /_internal/ping succeed from our egress path
- Auto-withdraw of prefixes and traffic failover to regional fallback on repeated health failures
- Ops runbook and rollback steps documented and tested
- Audit logs of config changes and peering events captured to customer-specified log sink or ours (per contract)

Example customer config snippet:
```
bgp:
  asn: 64496
  peer_ip: 10.0.0.2
  peer_asn: 65001
  announce_prefixes: ["10.200.0.0/24"]
  hold_time: 90
```

kai: Tests we need for acceptance:
- Unit tests for BGP session handling and peer auth
- Integration harness using FRR in a container to emulate customer router
- Canary run that measures latency/cost delta under customer egress vs our default path

Test harness example (local):
```
docker run --rm -it frrouting/frr:latest /usr/bin/bgpd -d -f ./bgpd.conf
./run_integration_test.sh --peer 10.0.0.2 --announce 10.200.0.0/24
```

priya: Prioritization note: for Q2 we scope to cloud VPC (AWS/GCP) where customer controls egress IP and BGP peering. On-prem physical appliances will be a ticketed pilot in Q3 — too many hardware trust and HSM considerations to do in initial launch.

sam: Security caveat: on-prem brings firmware/TPM/HSM considerations and we need attestation before GA. Recommend we keep on-prem in pilot.

natalie: Also add these acceptance items: ops runbook with exact CLI troubleshooting steps, and at least two internal or customer beta participants who validate config before GA.

alex: Action items and owners:
1) eng-platform (kai) — draft RFC with exact API contract, network interface schema, and integration tests
2) security (sam) — produce threat model and HSM/attestation guidance for on-prem pilots
3) solutions eng (natalie) — author customer config examples and troubleshooting doc + runbook
4) product (priya) — finalize launch gates, canary metrics, and prioritization (cloud-only vs on-prem)
Target: RFC in 7 days; canary plan within 2 weeks. @kai can you own the RFC?

kai: I'll draft the RFC and include smoketests. Will post PR by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: RFC draft created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/387 — alex, priya, sam, natalie, kai please review.

alex: Thanks. Quick note — include the metrics we'll measure during canary: token latency p50/p95, per-request cost delta, error rate (5xx + connection errors), and BGP flap count. Make thresholds explicit in the RFC.

priya: I'll add launch metrics and gate thresholds. Scheduling a 30m sync to finalize acceptance on Tue 10:00am PT.

natalie: :raised_hands: added to calendar.
